description: We are a 2-person team with AI & data science interests, who would like to contribute to NASA space exploration.
summary: Team GORA developed the Lunar South Pole Earth Analog Scoring Tool, an interactive decision-support web application that ranks Earth locations as field-testing sites for lunar excavation robots (such as RASSOR/IPEx-class hardware) and mobility rovers. Multi-million-dollar lunar surface missions carry high operational risk because hardware failures cannot be repaired remotely once launched; however, selecting an appropriate Earth analog site currently requires weeks of fragmented manual research across geological surveys, climate tables, and logistics estimates. Our tool solves this by evaluating candidate sites against a Lunar South Pole reference profile derived from NASA’s candidate Artemis landing regions. Sites are filtered for aridity and zero vegetation, then ranked using a transparent, hardware-weighted similarity score across five geological and environmental parameters alongside travel cost and logistics estimates. A parallel time-series module flags the optimal testing month(s) for illumination and temperature fidelity—de-risking pre-launch hardware validation and accelerating test campaign planning.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

The Lunar South Pole Earth Analog Scoring Tool evaluates candidate Earth locations—including Eureka (Canada), Meseta de Somuncura (Argentina), Salar de Uyuni (Bolivia), Nullarbor Plain (Australia),Ahaggar (Algeria), Peary Land (North Greenland), and the Pamir Plateau (Tajikistan)—against a reference profile derived from NASA’s nine candidate Lunar South Pole landing regions.

  • Hard Filtering & Weighted Scoring: Candidate sites must first pass a strict aridity and zero-vegetation filter (MODIS NDVI). Qualifying sites are then scored across five key parameters: grain size and particle shape, mineral composition and abrasiveness, terrain and slope, temperature extremes, and moisture/dust content, using a normalized distance-based similarity formula.
  • Hardware-Specific Weighting: Engineers can adjust parameter weights based on their hardware focus—prioritizing grain shape (0.30) and mineralogy (0.25) for excavation and haulage robots (such as RASSOR/IPEx-class systems), or terrain and slope (0.40) and grain shape (0.25) for mobility rovers.
  • Decoupled Temporal Matching: Alongside the main geological score, a separate time-series module (using dynamic time warping and correlation) compares each site’s annual MODIS/VIIRS land surface temperature and solar elevation curves against NASA LRO Diviner lunar diurnal waveforms. This flags the optimal testing month(s) without artificially inflating a site's overall geological similarity score.
  • Operational Output: The interactive web dashboard delivers ranked test sites, per-parameter breakdowns showing exactly where the Earth-Moon analogy holds or breaks down, and practical logistics and visit-cost tiers (Medium,High, and Very High—accounting for road access, permitting, and Arctic charter requirements).

Benefits & Intended Impact By consolidating planetary science, seasonal climate dynamics, and real-world field logistics into a single quantitative platform, our tool cuts test-site selection from weeks of fragmented literature review down to minutes. It enables robotics engineers, ISRU teams, and space companies to allocate testing budgets efficiently and catch mechanical or thermal hardware flaws on Earth before launch, where remote repairs are impossible.

Datasets, Tools & Development Stack

  • Earth & Lunar Datasets: NASA/NGA SRTM and ESA Copernicus DEM (terrain and slope); NASA MODIS and SMAP (land surface temperature, vegetation, and soil moisture); USGS, OneGeology, and ASTER (grain size and multispectral mineralogy); and NASA LRO (LOLA, Diviner, Moon Mineralogy Mapper) paired with Apollo soil mechanics literature for the lunar South Pole reference profile.
  • Software & Modeling: Developed as an interactive web application using transparent, interpretable weighted-sum and distance-based scoring algorithms alongside time-series similarity matching rather than black-box machine learning, avoiding overfitting across a small set of candidate locations.

Creativity & Factors Considered Rather than comparing Earth locations to a single crater coordinate or treating geological fidelity in isolation, our team integrated multi-criteria planetary data with real-world operational constraints (permits, road access, freight lead times) and decoupled seasonal illumination matching. We also explicitly accounted for physical and methodological limitations—including Earth’s inability to replicate 1/6th lunar gravity or hard vacuum,spatial resolution differences between Earth and lunar orbital sensors, and the necessity of on-site ground-truth validation.
